stack.__prompt__: Which stack? (wagtail = CMS site; django = plain Django app or API backend, no CMS)
stack.django: Plain Django application or API backend

__prompts__.client_name: Client name (used in branding and documentation)
__prompts__.author: Author / team
__prompts__.description: One-line project description, as a full sentence (it is printed as its own paragraph)

languages.en_ar: Bilingual English + Arabic (RTL support, translated fields)

frontend.api_only: API only, no server-rendered frontend (requires stack=django and an API)

multisite.multi: Multiple sites from one instance (site-scoped content and settings)

__prompts__.admin_url_prefix: Admin URL prefix (must NOT be 'admin'; no slashes)
__prompts__.django_admin_url_prefix: Django admin URL prefix [wagtail only] (must differ from admin_url_prefix and not sit under it)

use_2fa.__prompt__: Require two-factor authentication for admin accounts?

spam_protection.__prompt__: Spam / bot protection on public forms

rate_limiting.__prompt__: Rate limiting on public POST endpoints (django-ratelimit) + login lockout (django-axes)?

countries_app.__prompt__: Country data backend (apps/core/countries.py is the same contract either way)
countries_app.django_countries: KUWAITNET django-countries fork: a country field and choices, working immediately - no tables, no import, and the country-list policy lives in the data
countries_app.cities: apps/cities on django-cities-light: editor-toggleable countries, dial codes, nationalities, translated names, regions and cities - empty until 'manage.py cities_light' imports the GeoNames data
countries_app.none: No country data: forms carry no country field, and one international phone input instead of a dial-code select

notifications_app.__prompt__: Include the notifications app (admin-editable e-mail templates, per-language sending, e-mail log)?

newsletter.__prompt__: Include the newsletter app (subscribers, unsubscribe tokens, admin composer)?

newsroom.__prompt__: Include the newsroom app (articles as models with drafts and preview, served by one routable newsroom page)? [wagtail only]

forms_suite.__prompt__: Include the example contact form (validated, rate-limited, spam-protected, secure uploads)?

api.rest: Django REST Framework pack (/api/v1/, OpenAPI, JWT, throttles, RFC 9457 errors)
api.headless: DRF pack + Wagtail API v2 page/image/document endpoints (Wagtail only)

sentry.__prompt__: Sentry error monitoring (activated only when SENTRY_DSN is set)?

analytics.ga4_gtm: Google Analytics 4 / Tag Manager hooks (IDs from env)

media_storage.__prompt__: Where uploaded media is stored (the private/public split is the same either way)
media_storage.filesystem: Local disk: MEDIA_ROOT and PRIVATE_MEDIA_ROOT on the application server
media_storage.s3: Amazon S3 or an S3-compatible store (MinIO, Spaces, Wasabi) via django-storages

static_storage.__prompt__: Where collected static files are served from
static_storage.whitenoise: WhiteNoise from the application process (compressed, hashed filenames)
static_storage.cloud: The same object store as media, under a public 'static/' prefix (requires a cloud media_storage)

asset_pipeline.none: None: WhiteNoise already compresses and cache-busts, and there is no SASS/LESS to build
asset_pipeline.compressor: django-compressor with offline compression (adds a compile step to every deploy)

cache.redis: Redis (required in production when rate limiting is enabled)

task_queue.__prompt__: Background task queue (a worker process that runs work outside the request/response cycle)
task_queue.none: No background processing. The right default: a content site that sends a few e-mails inline does not need a worker, and a queue you do not need is another process to deploy, monitor and restart.
task_queue.huey: Small queue with built-in periodic tasks, backed by the database you already run (see huey_backend). Choose when you need real background work, retries and a schedule, but not Celery's routing, priorities or multi-queue scaling. One worker, a handful of task types.
task_queue.celery: The heavyweight. Choose only when you genuinely need routing, priorities, multiple queues, chains/groups, autoscaling or mature monitoring. Costs a broker, a worker, beat for schedules, and the operational surface of all three.

huey_backend.__prompt__: Huey storage backend (applies to task_queue='huey' only; ignored otherwise)
huey_backend.postgres: Uses the database you already run. No new service to deploy, monitor or back up - the queue is backed up with everything else. The right default: choose it unless you have measured a reason not to.
huey_backend.redis: Faster and keeps queue churn out of the database. Choose when task volume is high enough that queue writes are a real load on Postgres, and you already run Redis for cache. Queue contents are lost on a Redis restart unless persistence is tuned.
huey_backend.sqlite: Development and single-process use only. Do not select it for a deployed site - it does not survive multiple workers, and it contradicts the PostgreSQL-only rule in the standards.

task_broker.__prompt__: Celery message broker (applies to task_queue='celery' only; ignored otherwise)
task_broker.redis: Simplest, and you almost certainly already run it for cache and rate limiting. NOT a durable message broker: a restart can drop queued tasks unless persistence is tuned, and there are no publisher confirms or dead-letter queues. Fine when tasks are idempotent and losing one is recoverable - resize an image, warm a cache, send a non-critical notification. And no managed option here - you run it.
task_broker.rabbitmq: A real AMQP broker: durable queues, acknowledgements, publisher confirms, dead-letter exchanges, priorities and routing. Choose when losing a task is not acceptable - payment reconciliation, invoicing, anything a customer has been told already happened. Costs another server to run, monitor, back up and upgrade.
task_broker.sqs: Amazon SQS. Durable and redundant like RabbitMQ, but fully managed - no broker server to run, patch, back up or monitor, and IAM instead of broker credentials. Two real costs: Celery's remote control and events do not work over SQS, so 'celery inspect' and Flower's live monitoring go dark; and there are no broker-level priorities. Also set a visibility timeout longer than your slowest task, or SQS redelivers it and the task runs twice. Choose it when the project is already on AWS and you want durability without operating a broker.

docker.__prompt__: Include a Dockerfile (uv-based multi-stage) and docker-compose for local services?

ci.__prompt__: CI configuration (runs ruff, bandit, pip-audit, tests with the coverage gate)

deploy_target.__prompt__: Deployment target documented in the runbook

bootstrap.__prompt__: Bootstrap the generated project (git init, uv sync, makemigrations, pre-commit install, first commit)?
